title: Add benchmark-lab performance suites and reporting pipeline
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: standardize and expand the benchmark-lab performance test suites to cover throughput, latency, and memory profiling across representative workload runners, and wire results into the reporting pipeline used by the perf dashboard. This PR adds new YAML-based performance suite definitions, representative workload runners for chat/generation/embeddings, a lightweight profiling baseline harness, and end-to-end reporting glue to push summarized metrics into the reporting pipeline.

What changed (high level): added throughput and latency performance suites with parameterized scenarios; introduced representative workload runners that exercise ballistic and mixed workloads; added profiling baseline harness to collect cold-start and warm-run memory/CPU/KV-cache stats; implemented reporting pipeline step to aggregate suite outputs and upload metrics + artifacts to the reporting service; small docs and CI updates.

Testing: local runs of the suites were executed against the canary runtime on a 4-GPU test cluster (nv4). CI includes unit tests for the runners and integration e2e that runs a short subset of scenarios. Performance runs were verified manually for statistical sanity (min/median/95th).

Rollout & migration: this PR is backwards compatible with existing suite formats; new suites are additive and will not affect existing scheduled runs. The reporting pipeline step is gated behind a feature flag (benchmark_reporting_v2) in deployment configs.

Checklist: - [x] Add throughput/latency suite definitions - [x] Add representative workload runners (chat/generation/embeddings) - [x] Add profiling baseline harness - [x] Implement reporting pipeline aggregator step - [x] Add docs and quickstart - [x] CI coverage for runners and reporting stage

Release notes: Adds new performance suites and reporting pipeline integration to benchmark-lab; enables richer profiling baselines and representative runners for more accurate CPU/GPU/memory regression detection and cost modeling. No breaking changes.

review_comments: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Left a few nits on runner API (prefer explicit config object vs kwargs). Also question about retry semantics in upload_client for 500 vs 429.

Aisha Patel (author): Addressed runner API nit — switched to explicit RunnerConfig dataclass and added tests. Clarified retry behavior: 429 uses exponential backoff with jitter, 5xx will retry up to 3 times with linear backoff.

Hannah Lee (reviewer): Noted that e2e benchmark job timed out on first CI run; suggested splitting long scenarios into separate CI matrix entries. Also requested a short README section on how to interpret aggregated metrics.
Aisha Patel (author): Split the longest scenarios into separate CI matrix entries and added README section with examples for median/95th parsing and artifact links. Re-ran CI locally and in CI.
Omar Rahman (approver): Verified that profiling baseline outputs include the required fields for the dashboard and approved after CI passed.
